relevance_note: Five people in the cohort are described individually with A20 haploinsufficiency: "Five patients (cases 5, 10, 14, 29, 31) were classified as having Haploinsufficiency of A20 (HA20)", each with a printed TNFAIP3 variant, so the paper reports identifiable individuals with a TNFAIP3 variant.
method_note: Read the paper Markdown directly; no script transcribed any table, and every span below was re-checked character by character against the paper with text search. Scope: only the five HA20 cases (cases 5, 10, 14, 29, 31) and relatives of those people were extracted; the other 26 cohort patients (polygenic BD, TRAPS, CVID, ISG15 deficiency) got no rows and are counted in publications.cohort_size_as_stated = 31. Relatives in scope, all described in relation to an in-scope person: mother of case 10 ('Similar features in mother.'), mother of case 14 ('Mother also has autoimmune hypothyroidism.'), mother of case 29 (found to carry TNFAIP3: p.C657Vfs*14), maternal grandmother of case 29 and brother of case 29 ('Maternal grandmother, brother and maternal cousins had similar but milder symptoms.'). The 'brother' in that sentence is read as the brother of case 29 because the sentence is in case 29's family row; the maternal cousins are a plural group with no stated number, so no rows were created for them. Table 1 was read as patients-as-rows (its 'Case' column holds bare numbers, but the text uses 'case 5' etc., so the paper's own label is used); spans run from the patient's row label through the cell, and the plus/minus in-silico prediction cells ('D/B/D', '-/-/-', and the minus-sign version in the rows of cases 29 and 31) were not read as presence or absence of any feature. No stacked (' / ') cells occur in Table 1, so no value was dropped for stacking. The Table 1 row for case 12 is split over three Markdown lines by the conversion (a bold/HLA-B*51 artefact) and is out of scope. Contradictions found in the paper: (i) the text says 'five novel heterozygous variants in TNFAIP3' in five cases, but Table 1 prints two TNFAIP3 variants for case 10 (946G>A p.G316S and 1625_1626insGAC TACAGCAGAGGCC p.S548Dfs*128); both are recorded for case 10, and only p.S548Dfs*128 appears in the text's list of five; (ii) Table 1's 'Variant classification' column gives 3 for the TNFAIP3 variants of cases 10, 14, 29 and 31, which per the Methods means 'Class 3: unknown significance', while the Discussion says six of seven novel variants can be classified as pathogenic by ACMG criteria; the printed table value is recorded verbatim and the conflict is left unresolved; (iii) case 14 has 'chronic pulmonary interstitial emphysema' in Table 1 but 'chronic interstitial pneumonia' in the Results; both are recorded as observed features. Judgements made: 'redness of the eyes' (case 5) was mapped to the checklist item uveitis or other ocular inflammation; livedo reticularis (case 29) was mapped to skin lesions; headaches were not counted as central nervous system involvement; perianal ulcers were not counted as genital ulcers; 'recurrent tonsilitis' (case 31) was counted as recurrent infections; case 5's 'serial monitoring of inflammatory markers' was not treated as a report of raised markers; case 29's enlarged vestibular aqueduct and acute renal failure were left off the checklist because the checklist has no matching item. For the four relatives whose only clinical statement is 'similar symptoms', one vague observed row each was recorded and all checklist items are 'not reported'. is_proband is false for everyone (the paper calls no one a proband) and source_reference_in_review is 'not reported' (Table 1 has no source column and no previously published patients are described). HPO candidates were deliberately left null rather than guessed. Case 29's inheritance is 'inherited maternal' because the paper states his mother carries the same variant.
